new_libraries.name: Railuino
new_libraries.author: Joerg Pleumann, Christophe Bobille, Uwe Monreal
new_libraries.sentence: Control a Märklin layout through its CAN bus (Gleisbox, MS2, CS2) from an ESP32 or an Arduino with an MCP2515.
new_libraries.paragraph: Locomotives (MM2, MFX, DCC), functions, turnouts and accessories, decoder CVs, S88 feedback. Based on Railuino 0.9 by Joerg Pleumann.

new_libraries.name: SoftI2C_Shared_CLS
new_libraries.author: Felipe Verri <pipe.verri@gmail.com>
new_libraries.sentence: Allows the use of multiple non-programmable I2C devices with the same address while using around half as many GPIO pins.
new_libraries.paragraph: It does that by sharing the CLS accross devices and keeping a single SDA per device, which allows the use of multiple devices with the same address.

new_libraries.name: SunLocator
new_libraries.author: Clifford Farrugia
new_libraries.sentence: A lightweight solar calculator for sunrise, sunset and twilight times.
new_libraries.paragraph: Computes the local time at which the sun reaches any elevation angle (the horizon, civil/nautical/astronomical twilight, or a custom angle) for a given date and location. Pure C++, no hardware or network dependencies, works on AVR, SAM, SAMD, ESP8266, ESP32, RP2040 and more. Ideal for switching lights, blinds or relays based on daylight.
